title: The empty place, the reshimu and the Kav: a hiding that keeps everything
overview:
Chapter 13 is the *nimshal* of chapter 12's analogies. The *tzimtzum* of the empty place is a hiding of the Essence, like the teacher who hides his whole depth to teach in short: nothing is lost, the hidden light still surrounds and fills everything, and the receivers only do not see it. "At first darkness" is true only for those below; what the *Kav* reveals is the very light from before the *tzimtzum*. The light of the Essence is not even a *makif*; only the letters of the engraving come through, the way the Mitteler Rebbe's mind comes through a book that is paper and ink.

Then the *reshimu*: a power to limit the unlimited into one impression. The *kitzur* is not its true likeness, because the *reshimu* means everything is gone, so the analogies go step by step from "all there" to "all gone": the blueprint, the acrostic, the thrown stone that keeps moving like the planets, the hint. Still, the whole *Kav* comes from the *reshimu*, as the architect's blueprint builds the house, and nothing fashioned is missing from it. To think this through, says the chapter, is the whole of man.

sections.title: The nimshal: the tzimtzum is the teacher hiding his depth, not losing it
sections.summary: The *tzimtzum* called the empty place is a withdrawal and hiding of the Essence so that light can flow, like the teacher who hides all his depth to teach in short. The hidden light still surrounds and fills everything, inside it; it is only not seen by the receivers.

phrases.he: (יג) והנמשל מכל הנזכר לעיל יובן למעלה
בכללות ענין הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי,
שזהו בחינת הסתלקות וההעלם לעצמותו
כדי שיוכל להיות אחר כך בחינת השפעת אור כנזכר לעיל
ולא שנסתלק ונתעלם לגמרי
אלא כמשל הסתלקות והעלם בעצמו,
הידיעה של כל העומק והאריכות כששונה דרך קיצור כנ"ל

blocks.text: As was said in chapter 12: this is the *nimshal* of the analogy of chapter 12.

phrases.he: א"כ לפי זה
גם אחר כל ההשתלשלות דאבי''ע שעומד במקום פנוי זה,
הרי בחינת העלם אור העצמות
מקיף וסובב לכל השתלשלות דקו

blocks.text: As was said there, it is the same as with the teacher: the whole *pilpul* (debate) of the Gemara is *sovev* (surrounding) on the Mishna.

Picking up what came up before about *sovev*: *sovev* does not mean that it surrounds the outside of the whole world. It is *mamash* there, on each particular thing. *Sovev* does not mean outside of it; it is really inside of it. So by the teacher, the knowledge of the Gemara is not outside of his knowledge of the Mishna. It is actually inside of it. It is called *sovev* only because it is there in a way that is set apart: his knowledge of the Gemara is hidden, *sovev* on the Mishna, and it includes the Mishna in it as a parcel of it. It permeates the whole thing.

A *sovev* permeates the thing just as much as the *or pnimi* (inner light), the *memalei* (filling light), does. The only difference is that the *memalei* is felt in the thing, and the *sovev* is totally unfelt.

phrases.he: וכמו שהיה אור העצמות קודם הצמצום
ממלא את כל החלל ריקן ומקום פנוי הזה
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים,
כך גם אחר הצמצום
הרי ישנו לאור העצמיות כמו שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: It's still there, exactly the same way.

phrases.he: רק שלא נגלה למטה לגבי שפע המקבלים
phrases.en: It's just that it's not seen to the *mekabel*.

blocks.text: The light of the Essence is still really filling up the whole thing, the same as by the teacher. It is not that his knowledge really disappeared in any way. His knowledge still fills up his whole brain, and the smaller knowledge is still filled with it in exactly the same way. That is what Reb Hillel said: it does not mean that there is actually a hole in the light.

It is still there, exactly the same way. Only, as far as the *mekablim* go, it is just like when the teacher tells them the Mishna: they see only the outside of the Mishna. They do not get the whole *sovev* of the Gemara on it, and yet it really is there.

blocks.title: The Kitzur Shulchan Aruch
blocks.text: Even past the Mishna: take the laws of Sukkos in a *Shulchan Aruch*, and not even a *Shulchan Aruch*, a *Kitzur Shulchan Aruch*. In a *Kitzur Shulchan Aruch* you do not see the whole *pilpul*, but you are getting *mamash* the actual *psak halacha* (ruling), exactly according to the whole Gemara with all the arguments. Every single argument is there in the final halacha that you get. So it is really not gone at all. It is just not seen by the *mekabel* (receiver).

phrases.he: אבל לגבי עצמותו אין שינוי בזה כלל
phrases.en: As far as the *mashpia*, it's totally no *shinui*.

phrases.he: וכמו משל היודע כל האריכות להשיב לשואלו מיד,
גם בשעה ששונה לתלמידו בקיצור כו'.

blocks.text:
As far as the *mekabel* goes, it is really not gone; it is just not seen by him. As far as the *mashpia* (the giver) goes, there is totally no change.

The reader starts "like the known analogy", *hamashal hayadua*. "It's not *hayodea kol ha'arichus*?" "Oh, here it says *hayadua*." And the line is read again.

sections.title: Darkness first only for those below: the light came first, and the Kav reveals that same light
sections.summary: "At first, darkness" is true only for those below, who receive from the *reshimu*; in truth the light came first, as the teacher knows everything before he hides it. What the *Kav* reveals is the very light of the Essence from before the *tzimtzum*: "You are He".

phrases.he: ומה שכתוב ישת חשך סתרו
phrases.en: He surrounds himself with darkness, that he hides himself; he puts darkness around himself to hide himself.

phrases.he: וכמאמרז''ל ברישא חשוכה כו',
היינו לגבי למטה
phrases.en: as far as to the downstairs.

phrases.he: שנמשך רק מבחינת הרשימו שנשאר אחר ההעלם כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: He surrounds Himself with darkness: He puts darkness around Himself to hide Himself. And as our Sages say, *berisha chashucha* (at first, darkness). If you look at the actual order, as it was laid out here, really the light preceded the darkness. The darkness is not first; the light is first, really. What they say, *berisha chashucha*, is as far as downstairs.

blocks.title: The confused student and the teacher who knows
blocks.text: So as far as downstairs goes, it starts with the darkness. But as far as the real thing goes, it really started with the light. It is the same with a teacher. By the student it starts with a big sense of confusion. By the teacher it does not: the teacher starts off knowing the whole thing, and then he makes a concealment and has to tell him tiny little things.

phrases.he: וזהו אתה קדוש ושמך,
אור העצמי, קדוש ומובדל
ואתה הוא קודם כו'
phrases.en: You're before the world and you're after the world, exactly the same.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אני יהו״ה לא שניתי כו'
phrases.en: Is really no difference.

blocks.text: *Ata kadosh veshimcha kadosh*. A student stops him: "Over here it says *or ha'atzmi kadosh umuvdal*." "Okay, good. That makes more sense like that." And *ve'ata hu kodem*: You are before the world and You are after the world, exactly the same, as it says, *Ani Havaya lo shinisi*: there is really no difference.

phrases.he: משום דמה שמגלה עמוקות מני חשך
phrases.en: This thing that he reveals the *amukos* from the *choshech*,

phrases.he: והעלם זה אחר כך בהארת הקו,
הוא דווקא מאותו אור העצמות שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: this is really from the original *or ha'etzem*, which was before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: וזהו אתה הוא כו' וכידוע

blocks.text: This thing, that he reveals the *amukos* (deep things) out of the darkness, is really from the original light of the Essence, which was before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.title: The lost Gemara, rebuilt from the Mishna
blocks.text: This is like the matter of the Mishna and the Gemara. After there was a darkness they lost the original Gemara: certain things they did not lose, but certain things they lost, and they were able to reconstitute them out of the Mishna. But really it comes from the original light from before, which Rebbi put into the Mishna. When he put it into the Mishna he put the whole light in there; it is just that it was in a way that was contracted.

The next side opens here: this revelation of light later on is really from the original light of the Essence before the *tzimtzum*. And this is "You are He": *atah*, "You", is the revealed, and *Hu*, "He", is the hidden. *Atah*, the light after the *tzimtzum*, is *Hu*, the light before the *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: The light of the Essence is not even a makif; only the letters of the engraving come through
sections.summary: The light of the Essence around the chain is not a *makif* to an inner light: it is outside the category of influence altogether. What does come is only from the letters of the *glif glifu* in the *tehiru ila'a*, the measure He took of the receivers, the way the Mitteler Rebbe's book holds his mind and is paper and ink.

phrases.he: ואמנם לא נקרא אור העצמות שמקיף ההשתלשלות שבמקום פנוי כו', כמו בחינת מקיף לפנימי,
phrases.en: It's really not even called a *makif* at all to a *pnimi*.

phrases.he: כמקיף הכללי דקו
שמקיף לאבי''ע בשוה כו'
כי הרי עדיין אינו בגדר וסוג בחינת אור השפעה כלל,
phrases.en: It really has nothing to do with it.

phrases.he: גם לא להיות בחינת מקיף כו'
phrases.en: It's not really in a way of a *pnimi*, and it's not really in a way of a *makif*.

phrases.he: רק אור העצמות,
שהוא בחינת התגלותו כמו שהוא בעצמות
phrases.en: And it's still the same; it really didn't change.

blocks.text: As came up before, it is not even a *makif* to a *makif*: it is really not called a *makif* to an inner light at all, the way the general *makif* of the *Kav* is. The general *makif* of the *Kav* means the *machshava kduma* (primordial thought), a general *makif* to the inner light, which encompasses *ABYA* equally. That whole matter of the *machshava kduma* is *makif* equally, as was said a few minutes ago: it is *makif* in each place. But this light of the Essence is not really even a *makif*.

It really has nothing to do with it. It is not really a *makif*: a *makif* means that it is *makif* on something, and this really has nothing to do with it. It is not in the way of a *pnimi* and not in the way of a *makif*. It is still the same: it really did not change.

phrases.he: ולזה אנו אומרים הוא קיים
ושמו קיים
וכן ברוך הוא וברוך שמו וכהאי גוונא,
רק מבחינת אותיות דגליף בטהירו עילאה זה,
שהוא מה ששיער בעצמו בכח כו'

blocks.text: So we say *Hu kayam ushmo kayam*, and likewise *baruch Hu uvaruch shmo*: it is exactly the same as before. And this is a hint towards what goes on in *Ayin Beis* (the Rebbe Rashab's series of discourses): that from the original Essence of the light nothing went through.

The Mitteler Rebbe says that it does not go through, and the Rebbe Rashab said that it does go through, because he is talking about a different matter. As far as the light of the Essence goes, it has absolutely nothing to do with the world, and none of it goes through. It is only from the *glif glifu* (the engraving He engraved), and even that, not from the actual inside of the *glif glifu*, only from its letters. And not even that: it is from the *hispashtus* (spreading forth) of those letters, which is called the *or hamispashet* (the spreading light). And even what really went through from that does not *mamash* mean that it actually went through.

blocks.title: This book is paper and ink
blocks.text: It goes through the way, here, the *sechel* (intellect) of the Rebbe goes through these letters to us. But the very *sechel* of the Rebbe has nothing to do with us at all; it is on a totally different level, *mamash* totally incomprehensible to us. And even the little bit for which the Rebbe made a *glif glifu* to give us this book: he engraved this book inside of himself before it came out. That much is understood; otherwise where did this book come from? Even so, it does not mean that something from that actually went into this book. In this book there is nothing. This book is a piece of paper with ink, that is all it is. There is not one iota from the Mitteler Rebbe in it. And yet a *reshimu* is there, because the order of the letters is the same as the order of the letters in the first *glif glifu*.

That is why we can reconstitute a radiance from a radiance, and that is what goes through; so actually it does go through. What the Rebbe thought for us to get is what came to us. Take what we are learning now. You say: what do you mean, no light comes through? There is a light coming to us. But it is not that the actual light the Rebbe saw is coming to us. That is the whole matter of the *mashpia* and the *mekabel*: even in terms of spreading forth, what he spread forth of the light did not really come through here. It is only hidden inside this as a *reshimu*, and then it is reconstituted as a new radiance.

So it is only from the *glif glifu* in the *tehiru ila'a*: the Rebbe first of all had to estimate for himself what can these idiots understand. "What am I going to... I have to write a book, so I have to make a *shiur* (measure): what can these idiots understand?" You know what I'm saying?

sensitivity.reason: Has the Mitteler Rebbe call his readers "these idiots" (said twice) while estimating what they can understand.
sensitivity.publishable: So it is only from the *glif glifu* in the *tehiru ila'a*, which is what He measured within Himself, in potential: the Rebbe first of all had to estimate for himself what these readers could understand. "I have to write a book, so I have to make a *shiur* (measure): what can they understand?"

blocks.text: There had to be a *shiur*. He says: I am not going to be able to teach them the way I know it. So he had to make a *shiur*, and to make the *shiur* he had to look at them; he had to measure the *mekabel*.

That is the matter of the *kav hamida* (the line of measure), which is already before the *tzimtzum*: there is a matter of measure before the *tzimtzum*. They say that the *kav hamida* after the *tzimtzum* is really a matter of the *kav hamida* before the *tzimtzum*. In the *shiur* of the *glif glifu* He had to estimate what kind of *tzimtzum* He was going to make, and whom it was going to come to. Really that belongs only to the *kav hamida* after the *tzimtzum*, and here it is above having anything to do with it; still, the whole matter of the *kav hamida* after the *tzimtzum* came from here. And this is the *glif glifu* in the *tehiru ila'a*.

phrases.he: וגם זה הוא הנשאר בבחינת העלם והסתלקות קצת
phrases.en: Even by this, *haaros meshuarim* is also pretty much in a way of *helem* and *histalkus*.

phrases.he: דהיינו רק לפי ערך אופן הנצרך להשתלשלות אחר צמצום זה
phrases.en: It is only according to what he had to give over to us.

phrases.he: ודי למבין.

blocks.text: Even by this, the measured radiances are also pretty much in a way of hiding and withdrawal. It is only according to what He had to give over to us; it is only according to the *mekabel*. So much for the analogy of the teacher and the student.

sections.title: The soul in the body and the power of motion: affected, and not changed
sections.summary: By the second analogy the soul is bound to the body and affected by it, and still does not change when a limb fails; so the light of the Essence does not change when it shines in the *Kav*. He gets pleasure from the mitzvos without any change, and the third analogy says the same.

phrases.he: וגם על פי אופן משל הב' הנזכר לעיל דחיות הנפש בגוף,
שמשתנה ממהות רוחני למהות גשמי כנזכר לעיל
גם כן אין זה שינוי כלל,
שהרי כמו שיש קישור וחיבור לחיות הגשמי לחיות הרוחני
ממה שרואים התפעלות הנפש ממקרי חיות הגוף,
ועם כל זה לא ישתנה בעצם הרוחנית מחסרון התפשטות חיות אבר גשמי כנזכר לעיל,
כך אין שינוי בבחינת אור העצמות,
להיותו מאיר גם אחר הצמצום

blocks.text: And so by the second analogy too: even though you see that he is affected, yet really he is not affected at all.

blocks.question: If He is totally not affected, why should we do all the mitzvos? It says that the Aibershter gets a pleasure out of them.
blocks.text: Yes, but that does not mean that it makes any kind of change. It is the same as the soul: even though it gets a pleasure, it does not change at all, just as you see that when a physical limb is gone, it is not gone in the spiritual.

And by the way, this analogy is where these people are making a very big mistake: they think it is *ruchniyus* (spirituality). It is not; it is an analogy. The whole thing is an analogy, including the *ruchniyus*. The *ruchniyus* is also an analogy.

sensitivity.reason: "These people are making a very big mistake": a swipe at a group he does not name, who take the analogy for spirituality itself.
sensitivity.publishable: And by the way, it is a very big mistake to think this analogy is *ruchniyus* (spirituality). It is not; it is an analogy. The whole thing is an analogy, including the *ruchniyus*. The *ruchniyus* is also an analogy.

blocks.text: The *ruchniyus* and the *gashmiyus* (physicality) are the analogy, the *ruchniyus* included, as above.

phrases.he: גם שאינו רק לפי ערך ההשתלשלות
הרי יש ביניהם קשר וחיבור,
ועם כל זה בצמצום האור בבחינת הקו,
אין זה שינוי כלל באור העצמות על פי משל זה

blocks.text: Even though it is only according to the chain: in the analogy it is not really the original power of the soul that lights up later, and so in the *nimshal* too it is not really the same original light, only according to the chain. (Reading on, he stops himself: "Wait, wait," and reads the line again.)

phrases.he: וכן על פי משל הג' מכח התנועה בגשם
או כמשל התחכמות מכח המשכיל הנזכר לעיל
הכל עולה לסגנון א' כנזכר לעיל באריכות
phrases.en: It's all one thing, like we explained in chapter 12.

phrases.he: ודי למבין.

blocks.text: That was the second analogy. And so by the third: it is all one thing, as was explained at length in chapter 12.

sections.title: The reshimu: the power to limit the unlimited, and why the kitzur is not its likeness
sections.summary: The *reshimu* is a *koach hahagbala*, a power in the unlimited *Or Ein Sof* to squeeze all of itself into one impression, because He can do anything. The *kitzur* is not a true likeness, since it shows that something is left; the blueprint, then the letter for remembering, come closer to "everything is gone" while still keeping something.

phrases.he: ואמנם בבחינת הרשימו
phrases.en: But however, as far as the *reshimu*,

phrases.he: שמבואר למעלה, שזהו כמו הקיצור שכלול בו כל האריכות
הנה למעלה יובן מזה שזהו בחינת כח ההגבלה שיש באור אין סוף
phrases.en: that's to say, there is a *koach hagbala* in the *Or Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: הבלתי מוגבל בעצם
דהיינו להביא כל הארות אור העצמות הבלתי גבול בבחינת הגבול
phrases.en: He has the power to take this whole infinite light and squeeze it into nothing.

phrases.he: שזהו ענין הרושם
phrases.en: That's the whole *inyan* of the *roshem*,

phrases.he: שכולל בבחינת הגבלה מבחינת כל עצמות אור אין סוף,
phrases.en: it includes the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* in it.

phrases.he: כמשל הקיצור שכולל הכל כו'

blocks.text: So that is the matter of the *tzimtzum*. But as for the *reshimu*: what is this *tzimtzum* and *reshimu* upstairs? Especially the *reshimu*, which holds the whole length: it means that there is a *koach hahagbala* in the *Or Ein Sof*. There is this power.
He has the power to take this whole infinite light and squeeze it into nothing. That is the whole matter of the *roshem*: it includes the whole Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* in it.

phrases.he: כי הוא יתברך כל יכול,
phrases.en: He can do anything He wants.

phrases.he: וכלול בו גם כן מכח המגביל
להגביל ולכלול ברשימה א' מכל אור העצמות כו'
וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות.

blocks.text: He can do anything He wants.

phrases.he: אך הנה באמת אין זה דמיון אמיתי לבחינת הרשימו הנשאר בחלל ריקן ומקום פנוי הנזכר לעיל
כי הוא מורה שנסתלק משם הכל
phrases.en: Nothing is left.

phrases.he: ולא שנשאר איזה אור
phrases.en: Not that there was any light left,

phrases.he: רק שהוא בקצור וגבול,
phrases.en: except it's a tiny little light.

phrases.he: אלא רק בחינת רשימו בעלמא כו'
phrases.en: Nothing is really left, just sort of like an impression.

blocks.text: Nothing is left. It is not that there was any light left, a tiny little light. Nothing is really left, just sort of an impression; the actual thing is gone.

blocks.question: What does "for it shows that everything withdrew" mean, and what does "it" refer to, the reshimu or the kitzur?
blocks.text:
It is not like the soul and the body: in the body there is still some life from the soul. And in the Mishna the intellect of the Gemara is still there, just a little bit of it, the same original thing. "It" is on the *reshimu*. As an example for the *reshimu* he gave the matter of a *kitzur*, and now he says that the *kitzur* is not a good example of the *reshimu*, because the meaning of *reshimu* is that the whole thing is gone. It is just the opposite: the *kitzur* shows that something is left. ("Right, that's why it didn't make sense to me." "Now it makes sense.")

So that analogy is a good one to show that it is all there, *mamash* all there. It is not a good analogy to show that it is all gone.
blocks.outOfPlace: Asked in class 009 after lines 37 and 38 were read; it is about line 35.

phrases.he: אם כן הדמיון האמיתי הוא מרושם וציון קו קצר שעושין האומנין,
שכולל כל אריכות מעשה הבנין
ויותר מזה כמו האות לזכרון כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Even more is like the acrostics.

blocks.text: It is like the blueprint. Even more, it is like the acrostics.

The analogies he gives now each get progressively less: in each one it is more and more gone. In the blueprint the building is gone and you just have a bunch of lines. But then you say, wait a minute, you still have the actual shape of the building. The analogy of the teacher's *kitzur* to his student is there to show how the *tzimtzum* is not a real *tzimtzum*, how it is all there, even in the final *reshimu*. The Mishna represents the *reshimu* in which the whole Gemara is *mamash* still there: the *tzimtzum* is not a real *tzimtzum*, and the whole Gemara is really there.

Here the first analogy is an intermediary: the blueprint. A blueprint means that the whole building is gone and you just have a bunch of lines, but still the whole building is there, and you can see how it is all there, because it is *mamash* the shape of the whole building. So you say: this is still an intermediary thing, and now we have to go even more to the other side. First he gives you an analogy from one side that shows it is all there; then he gives you an analogy that shows it is all gone; and more and more in between, the intermediary.

And the Rebbe Rashab said that this really represents the chain of the worlds, which are analogies: first *Atzilus*, then *Beriya*, all the way down to *Yetzira*. In the first analogy it is not really gone: the Mishna is *mamash* the same thing as the Gemara, only a *kitzur*. In the second it is already all gone; a blueprint is not a house. Nonetheless it is the whole shape of the house.

And not only the *mashpia* can read it. "Let's say I'm not an architect or something like that": if he took a look at a blueprint and sat with it for an hour, he could figure out what it is supposed to be. So it is not gone even for the *mekabel*, really.

blocks.title: Every Good Boy
blocks.text: And even more so in the direction of all gone: like the letter for remembering. There you cannot even tell what it is. Like "Every Good Boy": you cannot figure out what it is just from knowing the letters. Nonetheless something is still left: those are the first letters.

phrases.he: וכך למעלה כתיב זכר רב טובך, העצמי
phrases.en: It's only a remembrance of the *rav tuvcha ha'atzmi*.

phrases.he: כו' וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: It is only a remembrance of the *rav tuvcha ha'atzmi* (Your essential great goodness). It is not the actual *rav tuvcha*, only a remembrance of it, like the letter for remembering.

sections.title: More hidden still: the thrown stone and the planets; and closest of all, the hint
sections.summary: The *reshimu* is like a thrown stone, moving by a power whose thrower is gone: so the spheres move by a hidden throw out of the nine outer vessels of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, and what you see in the moon and feel in gravity is that separated power. Closest of all is intellect hidden in a gesture or in writing: the *reshimu* is a separate thing in which the light is dressed.

phrases.he: ויותר בהעלם והסתלקות הוא כמשל הזורק אבן כו' כנזכר לעיל
וכך אמר בספר הבהיר
וכמו זרקא כו'
phrases.en: like he threw a stone.

phrases.he: שהרי בחינת הרשימו נשאר נבדל בריחוק מקום מעצמות האור וכו'
ונקרא כח הנעלם ברשימו זו בחינת העלם אור, נבדל מהעלם עצמות האור דאין סוף
כמו כח נבדל הנעלם בזריקת אבן
שבא מכח היד שכבר נעלם בעצמו כו'

blocks.text: Like he threw a stone. It is as if the actual original person is gone; that is what this analogy shows. The stone is still going with the original power, but the power that threw it is gone. It is like it is going by itself. And that is how the world is: it looks like the world is going by itself, like a thrown stone where you do not even see anymore who threw it.

Not only that: the power of the hand is not just that you cannot see it anymore; it is not continuing anymore. The actual hand is not throwing anymore. The power of the movement went back into the hand.

phrases.he: (וכדמיון כל הגלגלים וכוכבי לכת
phrases.en: like the whole physical universe with all the stars and planets

phrases.he: שסובבים מכח תנועה אלהי״ת הנעלם,
phrases.en: that are still moving around and around from the original throwing;

phrases.he: שבא בבחינת זריקה מאור וכח האלה״י דט' כלים החיצונים דמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: and this came from the nine outside *keilim* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

phrases.he: שנקרא זה כח הנבדל בחינת מלכות שבמלכות
הבא בערך ריחוק נבדל
phrases.en: in a faraway way,

phrases.he: ולא כמו הכתיבה באצבע או כח יד הפועל עצמו בנפעל
phrases.en: and not like the actual hand that's moving it.

phrases.he: שזהו גלוי עצם הכח בקירוב, שנקרא בחינת מלכות כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות)
phrases.en: And there you can see the hand.

blocks.text: It is like the whole physical universe, with all the stars and planets, that is still moving around and around from the original throw.

"You know, like the Big Bang thing." But it was not like the Big Bang thing. When you throw something and trace it back, you trace it all the way to the ground and say: "Wow, it blew up from the ground." It did not. It really started somewhere in the middle, from where you threw it. The same thing here: this throw happened five thousand seven hundred and sixty-three years ago ("Not 64?" "Well, not yet... actually 63, because we're just beginning the 64"). That is when it really started, in the middle.

sensitivity.reason: An opinion on science: he sets the Big Bang aside and dates the start of the universe's motion to 5763 years ago, as a thrown stone traced back only seems to start from the ground.
sensitivity.publishable: When you throw something and trace it back, you trace it all the way to the ground and say: "Wow, it blew up from the ground." It did not. It really started somewhere in the middle, from where you threw it. The same thing here: the motion of the universe really started in the middle, from the throw.

blocks.text: And this came from the nine outer vessels of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

So what he is saying to you here: if you go outside and look up and see the moon, you are actually seeing the power of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. Not only that, you are seeing the power of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* when you move, because you got that from the sunlight and such, and that is all from the *galgalim*. Not only that: you feel it pulling you down, the gravity and all that business. That is all from *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

You are *mamash* feeling the external power of the external vessels of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. That is what the throw actually is: it seems to be going on by itself, just like the stone, but really it is the external vessels of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. It is a separate power that comes in a faraway way, not like the actual hand that is moving a thing, where you can see the hand.

phrases.he: ומשלים היותר קרובים לזה הוא כמו הרמז שהשכל בהעלם בתנועה הגשמיית
שזהו נקרא בחינת הלבשה ותפיסא בדבר נבדל כו'
phrases.en: That the *sechel* is caught in a movement, which is a totally different *inyan* than a *sechel*.

phrases.he: וכן כשכותב שכל וחכמה בתנועת האצבע כו' כנזכר לעיל
כך למעלה, בחינת הרשימו בחינת דבר נבדל בערך,
שבו מלובש בהעלם מכללות אור העצמות כו'
ודי למבין.

blocks.text: The intellect is caught in a movement, which is a totally different thing from intellect.

It goes even farther when he actually writes it with the movement of the finger. That is connected to the finger, but the letter that comes out of it is basically just a bunch of shapes on a paper, and that can already be in a way of a throw: this book is a throw.
So here he basically went over the analogies of chapter 12.

sections.title: Everything comes from the reshimu: "nothing fashioned is missing from You"
sections.summary: Though the *reshimu* is a withdrawal of everything, the whole *Kav* comes from it, because it includes everything hidden; the light "breaks through" it the way the Gemara was rebuilt out of the Mishna. Nothing fashioned, the product itself, is missing from it, and in the *machshava kduma* He sees it all in one glance.

phrases.he: ואמנם מכל אלה יובן על כל פנים כללות ענין הרשימו
phrases.en: So from all these *meshalim*, even though one is a little bit more this way and one is a little bit more that way, when you put them all together, then you can understand at least the general *inyan*, what the *reshimu* was all about.

blocks.text: From all these analogies, even though each one is a little more this way and one a little more that way, when you put them all together you can understand at least the general matter of what the *reshimu* was all about.

phrases.he: דגם שהוא בא בבחינת הסתלקות הכל,
phrases.en: There is nothing left there.

phrases.he: ולא נשאר בה רק בהעלם גדול בחינת תכלית הקיצור והרמז כו'
או ככח נבדל כו', אבל
מכל מקום מזה עצמו בא ונמשך כל פרטי ההשתלשלות דקו
שנמשך מרשימו זו

blocks.text: Everything is really... there is nothing left there. Here he says very clearly that the *Kav* comes from the *reshimu*.

blocks.title: The Gemara broke through the Mishna
blocks.text: Later on, and in various places, it says that the light *boke'a* (breaks through) the *reshimu*. That does not mean that the actual light breaks through. It means that the light is really included in the *reshimu* and it is reconstituted. Like the Mishna and the Gemara: the Gemara that we have today broke through the *reshimu* of the Mishna. That does not mean that a guy read the Mishna and had a vision of one of the people from before the Mishna, who told him the whole Gemara. It means that it was included in there, and the original light, the stuff that you could not see in the *kitzur*, was actually reconstituted out of the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: כי ברשימו זו להיותה כוללת הכל בהעלם על כל פנים,
phrases.en: Since it includes everything, even though it's *b'helem*, nonetheless it's everything.

phrases.he: היא הנותנת שיוכל לבא הכל בהתגלות על ידי בחינת הקו עד סוף העשיה

blocks.text: Since it includes everything, even though it is in hiding, nonetheless it is everything.

phrases.he: וכמאמר כל היצור לא נכחד ממך
phrases.en: That all the *yetzur* is not missing from You.

blocks.text: "No *yetzur* is missing from You", *davka* from You. This is a part of the Rosh Hashana prayer. The usual translation of it is about knowledge: You are not missing knowledge of anything. But he translates it literally, and this is really what it means: there is nothing missing in the *reshimu*, and certainly not before the *reshimu*.

And he says here *yetzur*: not the manufacturing of the thing, but the actual thing itself. *Yetzur* does not mean the form; *yetzur* means the actual thing that was fashioned, the product, as was said before. The actual product is actually not missing there.

So it is as was said before: it does not mean, as people think, that it gets abstract. And it is not even like what was said, that the will for a sandwich is included in the will for *chesed*. In the *nimshal* we have to say that the actual sandwich itself was included there, because otherwise where did it come from? Here is a sandwich in front of us; you bite into it and say, "Wow, it's the actual sandwich." Where did it come from? On one side, to say that it is actually there is ridiculous. On the other side, to say that it is not there is *mamash* heresy against the unity.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 010 opens with this, finishing the point of the previous side before it reads line 59.

phrases.he: ממך דוקא,
phrases.en: Means in You.

phrases.he: שזהו הכל נעשה ונמשך בגלוי
phrases.en: that everything came out in *gilui*.

phrases.he: כמו שעלה ברצונו הפשוט בעצמות האור שלפני הצמצום
כמו ששיער בעצמו כו'
שהרי במחשבה קדומה זו ששיער בעצמו
הוא צופה ומביט הכל בסקירה א'
phrases.en: He sees the whole thing in one shot, everything.

phrases.he: דהיינו מה שנסקר בהעלם ובקיצור ורמז ברשימו זו כו'

blocks.text: *Mimcha davka* means in You: everything came out in revelation. The *machshava kduma* is after the *tzimtzum*, and the measuring within Himself is before the *tzimtzum*. He sees the whole thing in one shot, everything. It is all included there.

In the *machshava kduma* is the beginning of the reconstitution of what was already included, hidden, in the *reshimu*. And it was really already measured even before that, in the measuring of the *glif glifu*.

sections.title: The architect's blueprint, the marks of deep study, and the point that hides and reveals
sections.summary: The *reshimu* is the architect's blueprint, made so he need not think it all through again; and it is almost as if the blueprint, given to the contractor, makes the world by itself. It is a point of nothing that hides all that is above it and reveals everything to the receivers, and the *Kav* comes out of it like a *vav* from a *yud*.

phrases.he: והרי זה כמשל רושם האומן,
phrases.en: It's like the blueprint.

phrases.he: שממנו דוקא ידע לעשות כל אריכות מעשה הבנין בפרטי פרטיו מראשו לסופו
רק כדי שלא יתעלם ממנו טעמו ונימוקו בעצמותו לאריכות הענין,
הוא עושה לו רושם לזכרון
phrases.en: Therefore he makes a blueprint to remember his original plan,

phrases.he: שלא ינטה מזה
ולא יצטרך לעיין בעצמו מחדש
phrases.en: he doesn't have to look inside of himself anymore.

blocks.text: It is like the blueprint. What he is really telling you here is that the blueprint has a source in a previous blueprint that was in his head. So that he should not have to rethink it every time ("Oh yeah, how did I plan to make this wall?"), what does he do? He makes a blueprint to remember his original plan.

He does not have to look inside of himself anymore. But really, the blueprint originated before the blueprint. So here it says that what the *Aibershter* does is make the blueprint. And it is not that you say: why could He not just look inside Himself? He is already inside Himself. Here it is a little different, because it is almost as if He just makes the blueprint, and the blueprint makes the world.

blocks.title: The building robot
blocks.text: It is almost like a computerized blueprint. Say you had a building robot: all you had to do was put the blueprint into the robot, and then you can walk away, and the robot will build the whole building. It is sort of like that. *Adam Kadmon* is sort of like this: He made a primal thing of a man. These levels are not just levels; it is *mamash* like a being. He gave him over this thing, and now He can walk away.

blocks.title: The architect, the draftsman and the contractor
blocks.text: And by the way, if you look a little closer at the analogy, the blueprint is not really for himself. The way it is done, the blueprint is given over to a contractor. It is conceived by an architect, it is drawn by a draftsman, and then it is given over to a contractor, and the architect doesn't have to do nothing with the contractor. If he makes the blueprint properly, the contractor will not call him up every two seconds. It is all in the blueprint.

This matter of a blueprint, these analogies, can be applied to the whole *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of descending worlds), as we are going to see later. There are four people involved with a blueprint: the person who is going to build the house; the architect, who comes up with the concept of the house; the draftsman, who makes the form of the house; and the contractor, who does the making of the house. Later on this analogy is used over and over again, when we get into the different levels.

phrases.he: וכמו כן ענין הציונים ללימוד עמוק שבעצמו כו'
שזהו תועלת לידע מהם כל אורך עיון עומק עצמותו שיש לו,
פן ינטה ממנו כו'
phrases.en: without veering away from it.

blocks.text: In other words: if he wants to remember, instead of having to start thinking about the whole thing, he just thinks of the *tziyun* (mark) and automatically remembers the whole thing, without veering away from it.

phrases.he: וכך בחינת הרשימו הזאת
phrases.en: The same way, this *reshimu*

phrases.he: הכוללת ברמז ובקיצור מכל אור העצמות הנעלם בה,
הוא עצמו המקור לכל ההמשכות דקו וחוט
phrases.en: this *reshimu* itself is the *makor* to the whole *hamshacha* of the *Kav*,

phrases.he: בבחינת מקיף ופנימי מראשו לסופו
שיהיה הכל כמו שעלה ברצונו וחכמתו הפשוטה בעצמות אור אין סוף ממש כו'
phrases.en: that everything should be exactly like it was planned before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.text: The same way, this *reshimu* itself is the source of the whole drawing-down of the *Kav*, so that everything should be exactly as it was planned before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: וזהו מה שכתוב במקום אחר שהנקודה יש בה העלם והתגלות,
ב' הפכים
העלם מכל מה שעליון הימנה בערך,
phrases.en: is a hiding away of everything that's above it,

phrases.he: וגילוי הכל למקבלים נמצא ממנה דוקא
phrases.en: and everything that's going to come to the *mekablim* will come *davka* out of this *nekuda* of the *reshimu*.

blocks.text: It is a hiding away of everything that is above it. And everything that is going to come to the *mekablim* will come *davka* out of this point of the *reshimu*.

By the way, the concept of a *nekuda* is used in various places. One is the point of the *reshimu*. Another is the point as measure and particularity, if you know the points of *Tohu*. Then later on *chachma* is called a point. In each place the basic concept is the same, but it is a little different. This is not just like the point of *chachma*. Here it is *mamash* a total point of nothing, and it includes the infinite in it.

blocks.title: Did you get the point?
blocks.text: Say I tell you a whole long explanation, and then I ask you: did you get the point? Getting the point is not really the whole explanation, even though it includes the whole explanation. And it is really more than the whole explanation: if you really get the point, you can make ten more explanations on it, totally unlike the explanation you were given. The point includes more than the explanation, actually. And this point, by the way, is the point of *chachma*, which is a much lower point than the *reshimu*, a much higher point. And yet everything is included in it, and the whole thing will come out of it.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת הקו שנמשך מן הרשימו
שהוא כצורת ו' שראשו י'
phrases.en: that the head of the *vav* is a *yud*;

phrases.he: והולך ונמשך למטה
phrases.en: is like a point with a line coming out of it.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות

blocks.text: That is like a *vav*: the head of the *vav* is a *yud*, like a point with a line coming out of it.

blocks.title: The vav straight out of the yud
blocks.text: There is something in *Ayin Beis*, and then there is the *maamar* (discourse) of the Rebbe ("it's too bad I forgot which one it is"; he thinks it is in *Yud-Daled* or *Yud-Zayin*) that explains the two approaches. He says there that the Mitteler Rebbe is leaving out one letter of the Name here, and has the *vav* come straight out of the *yud*. And there he explains that there is an *olam hamalbish* (the enclothing world). What is the *olam hamalbish*? It is everything that could come out of the point: various lines. It does not have to be *davka* this *Kav*; it could really be many other lines. But here he is saying it is almost as if it comes straight from the point to the *vav*, the line.

blocks.title: The olam hamalbish, inside the reshimu
blocks.text: And the Rebbe said that according to this approach, and also since he is talking about a higher level, it is almost as if there is no *olam hamalbish*. According to the approach of the Rebbe Rashab there is an actual *olam hamalbish* in between, and the *Kav* comes out of the *olam hamalbish*. The point is that here the *reshimu* actually includes the *olam hamalbish* inside of it. It does not really get manifested, but it is really there: many different lines could really come out of this *reshimu*; it does not have to be only this *Kav*. "So, this is like a side issue over here."

sections.title: In sum: only a limitation in the Essence, and this is the whole of man
sections.summary: The *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu* and the *Kav* are only a limitation in the Essence so that everything can come into revelation; the *Kav* is a light born of the light hidden in the *reshimu*. To think this through is the whole reason a person is here, because it is what binds him to the Essence itself.

phrases.he: ובכל זה מובן כללות ענין הצמצום דמקום פנוי ובחינת הרשימו והקו
שהוא רק בחינת הגבלה בעצמות כדי שיומשך הכל בגלוי
וזה שכתוב כי עמך מקור חיים,
באורך העצמי
נראה אור, אור של תולדה,
שהוא בחינת הקו וכמו שיתבאר בעזרת ה׳

blocks.text: *Be'orcha nireh or* means a light that is a *tolda* (offspring). But it does not really mean that the actual *Kav* comes from the original light; it comes from the original light that is hidden in the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: וזה כל האדם,
phrases.en: And this is the whole reason that a person is here:

phrases.he: להעמיק דעתו בכל זה וכיוצא בו
phrases.en: to think about this.

phrases.he: מפני שמזה דוקא יבוא לכלל היחוד האמיתי בהתקשרות נפשו בחיי כל החיים העליונים,
שהוא עצמות אור אין סוף ממש
מטעם הנזכר לעיל ודי למבין:

blocks.text: This is the whole reason a person is here: to think about this. "That's the whole reason we're here." As he explained before, by understanding that the whole thing down here is nothing but a *tzimtzum* of it, he will be connected *davka* to the *etzem* (essence).

reviewQuestions.question: Why is the *tzimtzum* not a hole in the light, and how does the teacher who teaches in short show it?
If the *sovev* permeates the thing as much as the *memalei*, why is it called *sovev*?
Why is the light of the Essence around the chain not even a *makif*, and what does come through from it?
Why is the *kitzur* not a true likeness of the *reshimu*, and what do the blueprint and the letter for remembering add?
What does the thrown stone show about the world, and what are you seeing when you look at the moon?
If the *reshimu* means everything withdrew, how can the whole *Kav* come from it, as the blueprint shows?

notes.text: Class 008 is catalogued as chapter 12 (Tape019-Side1-Ch12); its last nine minutes read lines 1-12 of chapter 13 and are used here.
"That's what, you know, that Reb Hillel said": the Hebrew of the saying is garbled in the transcript; the block gives only what he explains it to mean (not a hole in the light).

Line 7: the reader first reads "hamashal hayadua" (the known analogy), someone points out it is "hayodea" (one who knows), and the reader's text has "hayadua". The chapter reads hayodea, which is the right reading here; the block keeps the exchange as dialogue.
"Rebbi put into the Mishna": he means the compiler of the Mishna; left as he said it.

"What can these idiots understand" (said twice, the Rebbe estimating what his readers can grasp) is put in an aside of its own (w736-796) and flagged "other"; the shiur and measuring the mekabel (w797-844) stay an explanation.

"These people are making a very big mistake, that they think it's ruchniyus": he does not say who; flagged lightly as other-groups, since it reads as a swipe at a group. The reread of line 22's tail (w1240-1262) is its own short explanation.
Line 46: "this throw happened 57... 63 years ago" means 5763 years; "we're just beginning the 64" dates the class to the start of 5764 (autumn 2003). The aside is flagged as an opinion on science.
Line 48: he reads "lo kmo achiza b'etzem" where the text has "lo kmo haksiva b'etzba"; the phrase follows the printed text.
Line 65: he reads "shelo yit'eh" (should not err) where the text has "shelo yinteh" (should not stray); the phrase follows the printed text.

Lines 73-74: the maamar of the Rebbe on the two approaches; he does not remember which ("I think it's in yud-daled or yud-zayin"). Presumably the Lubavitcher Rebbe (5714 or 5717), not the Mitteler Rebbe or the Rebbe Rashab; this is an inference and is kept out of the text. The reading of the line (w1207-1226) and its second reading after the digressions (w1486-1520) are one explanation with two audio entries.

Class 010 opens (words 0-147) with the sandwich example, "like we said before", from an earlier class (likely chapter 12); the transcript says nimshal twice where the first is probably mashal. Placed under line 58, whose point it finishes.
Line 76 is misread in the recording ("rashum shechakak bagilui"); he does not translate it, so its phrase has no English.
"Every Good Boy" is his example of an acrostic; he gives only the three words.

Line 10: he reads "ve'atah hu kadosh veshimcha kadosh, or ha'atzmus muvdal" (adding the prayer's second kadosh and dropping the kadosh before umuvdal); a student points out the text has "or ha'atzmi kadosh umuvdal", and he agrees. The block keeps the exchange.

Terms cut to twelve. Spellings used in the prose that translit.json lacked, for whoever merges it (ABYA, pilpul, mekabel, mashpia and Ayin Beis were added to it when the chapters were merged): ABYA (אבי״ע): Atzilus, Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya, the whole chain of the Kav standing in the empty place; pilpul (פלפול): Talmudic debate; the whole pilpul of the Gemara is sovev on the Mishna; mekabel (מקבל): the receiver, plural mekablim; only for him is anything gone, and only in that he does not see it; mashpia (משפיע): the giver; by him there is totally no change; Kitzur Shulchan Aruch (קיצור שולחן ערוך): the abridged code of law, in which every argument of the Gemara is there in the final ruling; psak halacha (פסק הלכה): a halachic ruling; Ayin Beis (ע״ב): the Rebbe Rashab's series of discourses, which holds that something does go through; or hamispashet (אור המתפשט): the spreading light: the spreading forth of the letters of the glif glifu; ruchniyus (רוחניות): spirituality; in the analogy of soul and body it too is only the analogy; gashmiyus (גשמיות): physicality; tziyun (ציון): a mark for a deep study of one's own; think of it and the whole thing comes back; tolda (תולדה): an offspring; the Kav, a light born of the light hidden in the reshimu.
